newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet :

TOP STORIES
Indian Express
SETBACK FOR BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY PRESIDENT

A Delhi court ordered the framing of charges against Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) President L.K. Advani under various provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act. The Central Bureau of Investigation has accused Advani of having accepted 3.5 million rupees in the form of a hawala (illegal money transfer) pay-off. The court order came as a severe setback for the BJP president, who had committed himself to staying out of electoral politics till the charges against him were dropped.
The Hindustan Times
FOUR JHARKHAND MUKTI MORCHA LEADERS ARRESTED IN PAY-OFF CASE

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested three former and one sitting Members of Parliament (MPs) of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, accused in the multi-million bribery case. CBI sources said the arrests were made following the interrogation of former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao on his alleged involvement in the case. The four accused, while being MPs in 1993, allegedly obtained illegal gratification as a motive for voting in the Lok Sabha (Lower House of Parliament) against the no-confidence motion moved by the opposition parties. Congress president Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister at that time.
Business Standard
TAX BREAKS TO BUOY CAPITAL MARKET

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced a clutch of tax concessions on investment in mutual funds, including Unit Trust of India (UTI). The move is aimed at boosting the capital markets by encouraging small investors. The minister, while replying to the budget debate, said the norms for foreign institutional investors (FIIs) had been further liberalised to permit them to raise their investments in corporate debt instruments from 30 to 100 percent. However, this would be restricted to dedicated debt funds. The minister also promised to make out a case with UTI and Life Insurance Corporation to step up their stock-market activity to ensure that FIIs alone do not emerge as the driving force in the markets.
OPPENHEIMER TO SHUT INDIAN OPERATIONS

Oppenheimer India Ltd, the local arm of the US-based Oppenheimer group, has decided to shut down operations in the country. The organisation has already retrenched staff at the Indian outfit. It would stop operations by the end of the year. However, the offshore India funds, already floated by Oppenheimer's asset management outfit, would remain operational. Sources said the decision was prompted by Oppenheimer's inability to succeed in Indian investment banking operations in the face of intense competition from other global majors.
CREDIT CAPITAL TAKEN OVER BY INFRASTRUCTURE LEASING

Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services has virtually taken over Credit Capital Venture Fund (India) Ltd by acquiring a 9.8 percent stake in the fund. It will make an open offer to acquire 20 percent of the outstanding share capital. This is first takeover bid after the announcement of the draft takeover code. It is also the first takeover of any asset management company in the country.
STATE BANK TO PUMP 500 MLN RUPEES INTO NEW SUBSIDIARY

The State Bank India (SBI) is planning to pump in 500 million rupees into the equity of SBI Commercial & International Bank Ltd (SBICIB). The SBICIB is the recast form of the erstwhile Bank of Credit & Commercial International, Bombay, which the SBI took over in 1994. The largest financial intermediary in the country has also become the first commercial bank to seek-in-principle approval of the Reserve Bank of India to float a new subsidiary to do business in the insurance sector.
Financial Express
MEASURES FAIL TO CHEER UP STOCK MARKET

The sops announced by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram for the capital market failed to shore up the general sentiment in the market. Market experts said they did not foresee any significant improvement in share prices when the stock markets would re-open on Monday. The Bombay Stock Exchange sensitive index closed at 3508.07 against the previous close of 3516.90, showing a net loss of 7.83 points. The broad-based National index, however, edged up by 4.03 points to 1581.56 from 1577.53 previously.
INDIA DEVELOPMENT BONDS TO BE FULLY REDEEMED

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said the government would fully redeem India Development Bonds issued in fiscal 1991/92 (April-March) in the current 1996/97 fiscal year. He said India needed $2.2 billion this year to redeem the bonds it issued in 1991/92 during a balance of payments crisis, when India faced a foreign exchange shortage.
84 FOREIGN INVESTMENT OFFERS APPROVED

Industry Minister Murasoli Maran cleared 84 projects involving foreign direct investment (FDI) worth 26.74 billion rupees. It approved FDI project of GE Capital Services India Ltd worth 8.75 billion rupees for providing financial services. The proposal of electricity generator CESC Ltd to raise $80 million through foreign commercial borrowings was also approved. Other notable projects that were cleared included 410 million rupee investment proposal of Rupert Murdoch's group company News Television India Pvt Ltd, Jeyjeth Granite Products Ltd's one billion rupee investment proposal for granite mining and trading activity and HCL Corporation Ltd's 522 million rupee investment proposal for software development.
NIPPON DENRO TO RAISE 13 BLN RUPEES FOR COIL UNIT

Nippon Denro Ispat Ltd is going to raise 13 billion rupee equity to part finance its 45.7 billion rupee expansion programme for its hot strip mill project. The remaining amount would be borrowed from 25 financial institutions and banks, both Indian and overseas. All necessary funds have been tied up, so also the technical collaborations. The project has been appraised by the Industrial Finance Corporation of India.
RIFT AMONG BANKERS WIDENS OVER PRIME LENDING RATES

Cracks in the Indian Banks Association have started deepening with several public sector banks refusing to follow the State Bank of India (SBI) in reducing their prime lending rates (PLRs). Some bankers even questioned the wisdom of SBI in taking such a decision. The SBI on Thursday lowered its PLR by 50 basis point for the second time within a short span of three months. The move evoked unfavourable response from bankers and even the highly profit-making banks like Oriental Bank of Commerce have expressed unwillingness to cut PLRs.
Business Line
FOREIGN FIRMS TO PICK UP STAKE IN UTI SECURITIES

Foreign broking firms are negotiating with the Unit Trust of India's (UTI) broking arm, UTI Securities Exchange Ltd, to pick up an equity stake in it. M.K. Khanna, Chief executive officer, UTI Securities Exchange Ltd, said a deal would be finalised soon as the talks were at an advanced stage. The proposed tie-up arrangement would enable UTI Securities to get access to international markets. There would also be no cost of setting up an independent establishment as it could make use of the existing facilities of its foreign partner.
LIMIT FOR BANK CREDIT AGAINST SHARES RAISED

Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, raised the limit for bank credit against shares and debentures to individuals from 500,000 rupees to one million rupees. The RBI said the monetary limit of 500,000 rupees for advances against shares and debentures to individuals, where the securities are required to be transferred in the bank's name, was also raised from to one million rupees. As per the RBI guidelines, banks should satisfy themselves about the marketability of the shares and debentures and the net worth and working of the company whose shares are offered as security.
SIEMENS TO FLOAT LEASING COMPANY, ENTER POWER SECTOR

Siemens Ltd has decided to float a leasing company in the areas of basic telecommunication projects. Chairman F.A. Mehta said the company had entered this field as it did not get payments in time from its customers in the telecommunications sector. He said the company would be a subsidiary and would have a substantial investment from Siemens. Besides, the parent company, Siemens AG, is also negotiating for equity participation in the three power projects in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Eastern India. Managing Director K. Pernstich said the total power generated from these projects would be 1,600 MW. Siemens AG would pick up 10-15 percent equity in these projects, he said.
The Observer
REVOLVING FUND TO TURN AROUND SICK UNITS BEING PLANNED

The government is planning to set up a revolving fund as part of a master plan for turning around sick public sector units (PSUs). The fund would have a huge corpus contributed by the government and would be extended to units which are recommended for revival. Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said the proposed master plan for PSUs turnaround would also envisage various options such as strategic alliance with joint venture partners and strengthening of management by inducting professionals on the board.
